    "chunk_summary": "NIST AI RMF §§1.2.2–1.2.4: defines risk tolerance and residual risk (adapted from ISO GUIDE 73), asserts tolerance is contextual and not prescribed by the Framework, sets normative guidance on risk prioritization (including ceasing development at unacceptable risk), and calls for integrating AI risk management into enterprise risk management."
  },

    {
      "id": "c_risk_tolerance",
      "name": "risk tolerance",
      "aliases": ["risk tolerances", "Risk tolerance"],
      "description": "An organization's or AI actor's readiness to bear risk in order to achieve its objectives; highly contextual and not prescribed by the AI RMF.",
      "anchor": "varied risk tolerances",
      "location": "1.2.2 Risk Tolerance"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_risk_prioritization",
      "name": "Risk prioritization",
      "aliases": ["risk prioritization"],
      "description": "Allocating policies and resources according to assessed risk level and potential impact of an AI system rather than attempting to eliminate all negative risk.",
      "anchor": "Risk prioritization may differ",
      "location": "1.2.3 Risk Prioritization"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_residual_risk",
      "name": "residual risk",
      "aliases": ["Residual risk", "residual risks"],
      "description": "Risk remaining after risk treatment, which directly impacts end users and affected individuals and communities.",
      "anchor": "Documenting residual risks",
      "location": "1.2.3 Risk Prioritization"
    },
    {

      "location": "1.2.4 Organizational Integration and Management of Risk"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_enterprise_risk_management",

      "location": "1.2.4 Organizational Integration and Management of Risk"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_risk_management_culture",

      "location": "1.2.3 Risk Prioritization"
    },

      "claim_text": "While the AI RMF can be used to prioritize risk, it does not prescribe risk tolerance.",

      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "does not prescribe risk tolerance",
      "location": "1.2.2 Risk Tolerance"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_tolerance_contextual",

      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "highly contextual and application",
      "location": "1.2.2 Risk Tolerance"
    },

      "anchor": "likely to change over time",
      "location": "1.2.2 Risk Tolerance"
    },

      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "define reasonable risk tolerance",
      "location": "1.2.2 Risk Tolerance"
    },

      "anchor": "counterproductive in practice",
      "location": "1.2.3 Risk Prioritization"
    },

      "id": "cl_prioritize_by_impact",
      "claim_text": "Policies and resources should be prioritized based on the assessed risk level and potential impact of an AI system.",

      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "Policies and resources should be",
      "location": "1.2.3 Risk Prioritization"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_cease_development",
      "claim_text": "In cases where an AI system presents unacceptable negative risk levels – such as where significant negative impacts are imminent, severe harms are actually occurring, or catastrophic risks are present – development and deployment should cease in a safe manner until risks can be sufficiently managed.",
      "claim_type": "normative",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "should cease in a safe manner",
      "location": "1.2.3 Risk Prioritization"
    },
    {

      "claim_text": "AI risks should not be considered in isolation.",

      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "should not be considered in isolation",
      "location": "1.2.4 Organizational Integration and Management of Risk"
    },

      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "AI RMF alone will not lead",
      "location": "1.2.4 Organizational Integration and Management of Risk"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_senior_commitment",
      "claim_text": "Effective risk management is realized through organizational commitment at senior levels and may require cultural change within an organization or industry.",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "realized through organizational commitment",
      "location": "1.2.4 Organizational Integration and Management of Risk"
    },
